info.title: Applicamp API
info.description: The Applicamp HTTP API. Errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`. Operations either are public or take the web app's session cookie (`session`); unsafe methods also need the `X-Applicamp-CSRF: 1` header and the app's own `Origin`. The agent API (`/api/agent/…`) takes a run's token instead (`run_token`), never a cookie.

get.description:
The issuer (this instance's public origin) and where its keys are. Only
when sandboxes run on OpenShell; not found otherwise.

post.description:
One completion of the `complete` role through the AI gateway, for the
run's account: refused when the account reached its daily tokens or a
spending limit (`ai_daily_limit_reached`, `ai_budget_reached`), and
when the run's tokens, with what its calls in flight reserved and this
call's worst case (its prompt at about four characters a token, and its
whole `max_tokens` answer), would pass its kind's budget
(`run_budget_reached`). The worst case is reserved before the call is
forwarded and settled to what it used. The run's tokens and cost grow by
what it used.

get.description:
The run, its kind, inputs, subject, limits, and the tools the agent may
call with their schemas and caps.

post.description:
At most 50 a call, each numbered by the agent, its message at most
2 000 characters, its data at most 8 KB, none with a NUL character; all
or none are recorded. A run keeps at most 5 000 events.

The agent's outcome and summary (checked against the kind's output
schema: `invalid_summary`). The token stops working; the server ends the
run once the sandbox is gone.

One call of one of the kind's tools. A tool the kind does not have is
not found; arguments that do not match its schema are refused
(`invalid_arguments`, saying where) and do not count; past its cap the
call is refused (`tool_cap_reached`).

get.description:
Every board, approved, waiting for the owner, paused or declined,
highest average salary first: the mean of the stated salaries of its
engineering jobs open to where the person lives (30 days), in euros a
year; a country-scoped board with fewer than 10 by its country's typical
pay; no salary data last. With the person's totals per board (7 and 30
days) and whether they manage the boards.

get.summary: The admin overview of the job boards.
get.description:
Totals (being read as job sites and companies, waiting for you, being
checked, not allowed, paused), what happened over the last 7 days from the
discovery runs and approvals the app recorded, and every board that is not
read, paused or declined with its stage and what it waits for. Board owners
only: anyone else gets 404.

Searched (`q`: a name, a site's host or a tag) and filtered (`show`) on the
server, so thousands of boards never reach the client at once. Ordered by
the jobs read at the last read, most first, then by id; the cursor is the
last line's place in that order, so a page never repeats or skips a board.
Board owners only: anyone else gets 404.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Matches a name, a site's host or a tag, ignoring case.

parameters.name: show
parameters.description: What to show; every board when left out.

get.description:
The person's searches and the discovery runs, newest first, ten a page.
A search has its funnel: jobs read, given a quick look, read in full,
good matches, kept with a note, and why the others were left out (with
the matches, they add up to the jobs read). Each run has what it scanned
on every board: jobs read, passed their requirements, given a quick
look, read in full by the AI, matched, the AI's cost, or why a board was
skipped (its polling limit), failed or was read in part; and what a
discovery check found. Filter by board or by search.

get.summary: How the job store is doing.
get.description:
Jobs stored, new in the last 7 days, sites read today and the reads that
failed, for the board owners. No job is shown here.

post.description:
Its site becomes a candidate, checked in the background (robots rules,
terms, a feed, a sample), and waits for the owner: nothing is read for
jobs before it is approved. At most 10 a day. The same site twice
answers the board already there (200).

200.description: That site is already a board.

202.description: Added as a candidate; the check runs.

get.description:
Its ranking, config, terms and the automatic check (robots rules, the
terms' sentences, sample jobs, the proposed attribution), and whether it
can be approved now.

post.description:
From then on searches read it. Only a candidate or a paused board with
no blocker: nothing the research found forbids reading it, its key is
set if it needs one, its config reads its kind, and its check (of the
feed's host) found robots rules that allow the feed. The problem names
the first blocker and says what exactly. Board owners only.

409.description: `not_waiting`: it is approved or declined; else its first blocker: `terms_forbid`, `robots_disallowed`, `needs_key`, `needs_permission`, `no_endpoint`, `config_invalid`, `check_needed`; the detail says what exactly

post.description:
Reads its robots rules (for its feed's host), terms page and a sample of
its jobs, once each, in the background; the board shows the result.
Board owners only.

202.description: The check runs in the background.

put.description:
The whole config, validated for the board's kind (or the new `kind`, as
a check's proposal gives it); unknown keys refused; a problem names the
field. An approved board's new feed must still be allowed by the robots
rules its check found. The seed list never overwrites it again. Board
owners only.

400.description: `invalid_config`: the detail names the field and says what is wrong

409.description: `robots_disallowed`: an approved board's new feed is not allowed by its robots rules; `kind_locked`: an approved board keeps its kind

post.description: It is never read, and says why. Board owners only.

put.summary: Set a job board's API key.
put.description:
One value per parameter its config's `key` names, each 1 to 200 visible
characters. Stored sealed with the instance secret and sent only to the
host its config reads now; never returned (the board says "key set").
Board owners only.

409.description: `no_key_needed`: its config names no key; `no_endpoint`: it has no address to send it to

delete.summary: Remove a job board's API key.
delete.description: Searches stop reading it until a key is set again. Board owners only.

post.description: Searches stop reading it until it is approved again. Board owners only.

get.summary: The permission email for a board.
get.description:
Addressed to the board's contact when its check found one. Fills in the
board's name, what Applicamp would read, the link back, the reading
frequency (at most hourly), no reposting and dropping closed jobs. It is
signed "Applicamp": the app does not know the owner's name. The app never
sends it: the owner sends it from their own mailbox. Board owners only.

404.description: `not_found`: no such board, or not a board owner

post.description:
A permission only after it was asked (a choice needs no email). "yes" approves the board through the approve
path (the note "They said yes on <date>" is kept): the terms and
permission blockers are cleared, but robots rules that forbid the feed and
a missing key still refuse it (409, nothing recorded). "no" declines it
through the decline path with the reason "They said no on <date>". Board
owners only.

200.description: Recorded: the board, approved or declined.

404.description: `not_found`: no such board, or not a board owner

409.description: `not_asked`: nothing was asked yet; `not_waiting`; or the first blocker that remains when the answer is yes

post.summary: Record that the permission email was sent.
post.description:
Stores the date; asking twice keeps the first date. The app sends
nothing. Board owners only.

404.description: `not_found`: no such board, or not a board owner

409.description: `not_waiting`: the board is read or declined

post.description:
A declined board is put back where it was: approved when it was
approved before (the owner stopped reading it), else waiting for the
owner. Its decline reason is cleared. Board owners only.

404.description: `not_found`: no such board, or not a board owner

get.description:
The companies whose jobs keep fitting the signed-in person (at least two
matches, or one they shortlisted, in the last eight weeks), each with
reasons traced to the postings they come from, and the companies they
watch, with their job board, open jobs and last check. Suggestions are
worked out from the person's matches, with no model.

200.description: The suggestions and the watched companies.

post.description:
Paste the company's careers page (or a link to its Greenhouse, Lever or
Ashby board): the company is added as one you watch, and its job board is
looked for the same way as for a suggestion. The page is read only where
its robots.txt allows. 409 `watch_limit_reached` past 20.

202.description: Watching; its board is being looked for.

post.summary: Give a watched company a careers page.
post.description:
For a watch whose job board could not be found: the page is looked at the
same way (a Greenhouse, Lever or Ashby board, or schema.org `JobPosting`
data), where its robots.txt allows.
Hides it for good: it is never suggested again.

Its job board is not read any more. It is not suggested again; watch it
again by pasting its careers page.

Puts it back among the suggestions, as it was. Only for a company the
person said "Not interested" in (404 otherwise).

Moves it to the watched companies and looks for its job board in the
background: the board a posting came from, else the careers page on its
own site (robots.txt respected). At most 20 watched companies (409
`watch_limit_reached`).

202.description: Watching; its board is being looked for.

get.description:
The PDF versions and the drafts still being reviewed, across all the
opportunities of the account (the ones put away included: a PDF is what was
sent), newest first. Never calls a model.
Version 0 and no answers until they answer a question.

put.description:
All the answers at once, as the interview or an edit leaves them; a
question left out is unanswered. Values are trimmed and blank ones
removed. Lists over their limit (5 roles; 10 places, things to avoid and
must-haves), a currency that is not ISO 4217 or a choice that does not
exist are refused. Every save, even of the same answers, is a new version.

200.description: The goals, saved, at their new version.

get.description:
The account behind the session cookie, with the providers linked to it.
Never a token.

The sites the app can read for the signed-in person, in groups: Remote,
worldwide; Europe; their country; By trade; Startups and all-jobs sites.
Each is On or Off: the app sets it from their goals (where they want to
work, remote or not, where they live, their roles and skills against what
the site offers) until they choose themselves. `q` finds a site by name;
`show` keeps the sites that are On, remote, in Europe, in their country or
for one trade. Also: the sites that do not allow apps to read them, and
how many company hiring pages the app reads besides.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Only sites whose name has this in it, ignoring case.

parameters.name: show
parameters.description: What to show; all sites when left out.

put.summary: Turn a site On or Off.
put.description:
The person's own choice: the app does not change it again, even when
their goals change. A site that needs a key cannot be turned On until the
key is set (409 `needs_key`); a site that is not on the list is 404.

get.description:
Every opportunity of the signed-in person, newest first, except the
dismissed ones ("Not for me") and the hidden ones (they fail a hard
requirement; `hidden=true` lists only those, with the reason). Filter by
stage, by text in the role, company or place, to the new ones, or to the
ones proposed to the person (`proposed=true`, best match first).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Only those whose role, company or place contains this.

parameters.name: new
parameters.description: Only the new ones (Found, never opened).

parameters.name: hidden
parameters.description:
Only the hidden ones: found before the requirement rules, they fail
one. Left out otherwise.

parameters.name: proposed
parameters.description:
Only the ones proposed to the person (Found, a match of 75 or more,
open to them), best match first.

post.summary: Add a job by its link.
post.description:
A Greenhouse, Lever or Ashby posting is read from the board's public API
(title, company, place, pay, description), and that company's board is
searched from then on. Any other link becomes an opportunity with the
link and the title and company given (typed later if not): the server
never fetches it. The same posting twice answers the one already there
(200).

200.description: That posting was already in the pipeline.

get.description:
One of the signed-in person's, dismissed ones included. Anyone else's is
not found.

patch.description:
Its stage, next step, notes, "Not for me" (`dismissed`), or that it was
opened (no longer new). Title, company and place can be typed only for
one added by a link to a site that is not a job board. Shortlisting a job
starts its preparation when the person's Autonomy goal lets the app
prepare by itself; moving it back to Found or "Not for me" stops it.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: A language tag such as `pt-PT`; English when left out.

409.description: `not_editable`: its title, company and place come from the job board

get.description:
What a tailored CV for it would be based on, as it is now: the company's
site (or that the person has to type it), the facts read on it, what the
job wants most, the questions where the profile is thin, what each step
costs and what was spent, and what the app does by itself for it. **Never
calls the model and never fetches**; opening it may start the preparation
of a shortlisted job that was never prepared, or its next step once what it
waited on is done (it runs in the background). Another account's
opportunity is not found.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: A language tag such as `pt-PT`; English when left out.

delete.description: It stays removed on later reads, and Undo (`…/restore`) brings it back.

post.summary: Undo a removal: the fact is back.
Read what the person pasted from the company's site.
post.description:
When the site cannot be read (it asks apps not to, or does not answer),
the person can paste what it says. The text is read like one of the
site's pages (**one model call**): each fact must quote it, or it is left
out; it replaces the company's facts as a read does. It counts toward the
20 company reads a day. The text is data, never instructions. A CV made
before does not change: Write it again uses the facts.

200.description: The brief, with the facts of the pasted text.

post.description:
**One small model call** reads the answer as Grill me does, with the same
checks: each fact quotes the person's own words and says nothing they or
their profile do not. The facts wait on the position the question is about
(the most recent one when it names none: `defaulted`), to be kept, fixed or
dropped with Grill me's endpoints (`/api/v1/profile/grill/proposals/{id}/…`).
Nothing reaches the profile until a click.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: A language tag such as `pt-PT`; English when left out.

post.description:
For a question about a skill: the skill is recorded as not theirs (like a
dismissed suggestion), and neither it nor this question is asked about
again. No model call. A question with no skill is a 400.

400.description: `no_skill`: the question is not about a skill

post.summary: Skip a question: it is hidden for this opportunity. No model call.
Read about the company and compare the job.
post.description:
Reads the company's own pages (the posting, its home page and up to five
pages it links to about the company; the same site only, where robots.txt
allows) and makes the facts: **one model call**, reused for 30 days per
company unless `again=true`. Then compares the posting with those facts and
a compact profile: **one more call**, reused until the posting changes.
Each fact must quote the page it cites, or it is left out. At most
20 company reads per account per UTC day, fetches included.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: A language tag such as `pt-PT`; English when left out.

parameters.name: again
parameters.description: Read the company's pages again, even though its facts are fresh.

put.description:
Only its host (and port) is kept, on the company: it is asked once, and
wins over every guess. The address must be one the server may ask (a public
https address). A different site than before forgets the facts read on the
old one.

get.summary: The tailored CV of an opportunity.
get.description:
The latest draft with each line's sources, marks and reasons, what was
left out, the job's keywords against it, the approved versions, the caps
and the spend. **Never calls the model.** Another account's opportunity is
not found.

post.summary: Draft a CV for this job.
post.description:
**Up to four model calls**: the draft on the `write` role (again with more
room only when its answer is cut off), the second look at what the job
wants, and the app's fix of what the check flags. From the posting, what
the job wants, the company
facts not removed and the profile; each line cites the profile sources it
comes from, and the server then checks that it says nothing they do not.
The model never sees a name or contact details. Needs the opportunity at
Shortlisted or later. When the job was never compared, the company is read
and the job compared first (up to two more calls, as Read does), so the
draft knows what the job wants; a company that cannot be read does not stop
the draft. At most 10 drafts per opportunity and 20 per account per UTC
day; nothing retries past a limit. A new draft puts the earlier unapproved
one away.

200.description: The CV, with the new draft.

post.description:
Refused (409 `lines_flagged`) while any line or skill cannot be traced to
the profile. The draft is frozen, its text rendered as a PDF with the
`template` and `length` asked for (the preview's when left out, else
Clean on 1 page), the PDF read back out and compared with the CV, and the
PDF kept as the next version: all or nothing. The preview's PDF is kept
as it is when the draft has not changed since it was made, its layout is
the one asked for and its read-back passed. If it does not fit the length (`cv_doesnt_fit`) or the
read-back finds it lacking (`cv_pdf_check_failed`, with the reasons, one
per line), nothing is approved. Contact details are read from the profile
again. No model call.

requestBody.description: The look of the PDF; optional.

post.description: An approved version cannot be discarded. No model call.

The position is no longer named under "Earlier", in the PDF or on the
page. It stays among what the CV left out, and putting it back shows it
again. The preview is made again. No model call. Only a draft can change.

patch.summary: Change one line of a draft.
patch.description:
`{text}` edits it: the new text is checked against the **same sources**
(an edited line that is not a summary drops its company-fact citations,
and a bullet drops another position's), and the app's question about it,
if any, goes. The preview is made again.
`{remove: true}` removes the line (a position left with no line goes to
"left out"), or the skill. No model call. Only a draft can change.

404.description: `not_found`: no such opportunity, draft or line

post.summary: "Yes, keep it", or "It's true" in the person's words.
post.description:
`{proposal: true}` keeps the fact the app proposed for a flagged line
(its question's, else the line's own words) on the line's position as a
**confirmed assumption**, based on this CV draft; refused
(`cannot_keep`) for a company fact used as an achievement, another job's
line, or one longer than a fact (its `waiting` item says which). `{text}`
keeps the person's own words as a fact (its `quote` is the text; `area`
defaults to `results`), as Grill me's Keep does. Either way the line is
checked again with that fact as a source (and none another position's or
a company's), and the preview is made again. For a skill it adds the
skill to the profile instead. A summary or headline puts the fact on the
most recent position. No model call.

200.description: The CV, after the line was checked again.

post.summary: See the draft in another layout, or make its PDF again.
post.description:
Renders the draft's text with the `template` and `length` asked for (what
the preview has when left out) and keeps it as its preview. **No model
call.** What the read-back finds is a note, never a refusal. Refused when
it does not fit the length (`cv_doesnt_fit`): the preview stays as it was.
Only a draft has a preview to change. At most 30 a day per account
(`cv_previews_daily_cap`).

200.description: The CV, with the new preview.

get.summary: The PDF of a draft's preview.
get.description:
`Content-Type: application/pdf`, shown inline, named
`<Name> CV - <Company> (draft).pdf`; `?download=1` serves it as an
attachment. Never cached, never sniffed. A draft with no preview, and
another account's, are not found.

parameters.name: v
parameters.description:
Anything: lets the page ask for the newest preview (it is never
cached).

post.summary: Put back what the draft left out, as the profile has it.
post.description:
`{position}` puts a position left out back with up to three of its lines
(highlights, else kept facts, else its summary), word for word; `{source}`
puts one left-out line back on its position. Each cites its own source, so
it passes the check. No model call.

200.description: The CV, with it put back.

404.description: `not_found`: no such draft, position or line

post.summary: Undo an approval, for a moment.
post.description:
Within 15 seconds of approving, before the cover letter that comes next
starts, the draft becomes a draft again: its PDF version goes, the
letter waits for the CV again, and the preview is made again. Refused
after that (`too_late`), or when it is not approved (`not_approved`). No
model call.

200.description: The CV, with the draft back.

post.summary: Make another version of the approved CV.
post.description:
The latest approved draft's text, rendered with `template` and `length`
(what the newest version has when left out), read back, and kept as the
next version. **No model call.** The earlier versions are untouched. Refused
when the text does not fit the length (`cv_doesnt_fit`) or the read-back
finds the PDF lacking (`cv_pdf_check_failed`, with the reasons, one per
line). At most 20 versions per opportunity.

200.description: The CV, with the new version.

get.description:
`Content-Type: application/pdf`, shown inline, named
`<Name> CV - <Company>.pdf`. `?download=1` serves it as an attachment and
sets the version's `downloaded_at`. Never cached, never sniffed. Another
account's version is not found.

parameters.name: download
parameters.description: `1` serves it as an attachment and records the download.

get.summary: The cover letter of an opportunity.
get.description:
The latest draft with each paragraph's tags and sources and each
sentence's reasons, the job's own questions and their answers, the PDF
versions, the caps and the spend. **Never calls the model.** Another
account's opportunity is not found.

post.summary: Write the cover letter for this job.
post.description:
**One model call.** From the posting, what the job wants, the company
facts not removed, the profile, the approved CV's words and the job's own
questions; each sentence cites the sources it comes from, and the server
then checks that it says nothing they do not. The model never sees a name
or contact details. Needs the CV of this job approved. At most 10 letter
drafts per opportunity and 20 per account per UTC day, counted apart from
CV drafts; nothing retries past a limit. A new draft puts the earlier
unapproved one away.

200.description: The letter, with the new draft.

patch.summary: Write your own answer to one of the job's questions, or leave it out.
patch.description:
The answer is the person's own words, so it is not checked against the
profile; it is text to copy into the application, not part of the PDF.

post.summary: Approve the letter and make its PDF.
post.description:
Checked again now: refused while anything is flagged or a job question is
still open (`letter_flagged`). The letter is then rendered on one page with
the CV's template stack, read back (every paragraph, the name and the email
must come out of the PDF as text), and kept as the next version in the
same transaction that approves; if any step fails nothing is approved.
**No model call.** The answers to the job's questions are not in the PDF.

patch.description:
The new text is checked against the sentence's sources again; removing it
takes it out of the letter. Only a draft can change.

404.description: `not_found`: no such opportunity, draft or sentence

post.summary:
"It's true": keep the person's own words as a fact on their profile and
cite it from the sentence.
post.description:
The words (up to 300 characters) become a fact kept on the position the
sentence is about (else the most recent), a source the sentence cites, and
the sentence is checked again with it. The profile keeps them for every
later letter and CV.

200.description: The letter, after the sentence was checked again.

get.summary: The PDF of a letter version.
get.description:
`Content-Type: application/pdf`, shown inline, named
`<Name> Cover letter - <Company>.pdf`. `?download=1` serves it as an
attachment and sets the version's `downloaded_at`. Never cached, never
sniffed. Another account's version is not found.

parameters.name: download
parameters.description: `1` serves it as an attachment and records the download.

post.summary: Prepare this job by itself, again.
post.description:
Queues the preparation from its first step (each step that is already done
is skipped without a model call): after Stop, after a cap or a limit
stopped it, or after a step failed (Try again). Needs the job at
Shortlisted or later, a model, and an Autonomy goal other than "Find
only". Runs in the background; the brief says where it is.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: A language tag such as `pt-PT`; English when left out.

200.description: The brief, with the preparation queued.

post.summary: Stop preparing this job by itself.
post.description:
What is still to run does not run; what was made stays (a draft is still
there to approve or discard). "Prepare by itself" starts it again.

200.description: The brief, with the preparation stopped.

get.description: Empty (and no `source`) until they import or write one.

put.description:
The whole profile, as edited by hand. Values are trimmed and empty ones
removed; a value over its length, a date not like `2020`, `2020-03` or
`2020-03-15`, or a list of more than 200 entries is refused.

get.summary:
The wizard's state: the portrait if one was made for this version of the
profile, the latest employers, what the person said, and the pending
changes. Never calls the model.

put.summary:
"Is this accurate?": stored; the questions that follow use it to decide
how many to ask.

Settle a change: *It's true*, *Fix* (or *Edit*) with a new value that is
checked again against their words, or *Use my own words*, which puts the
exact text they wrote into the field (for the summary, their whole
answer). Nothing is saved yet.

delete.summary: Take a change out of what will be saved.

post.summary: Read one past employer's website again, after it could not be read.
post.description:
Only that employer: **one model call**, counted toward the day's limit
like any other. Whatever comes of it is shown on that employer's row, and
the portrait is not touched; *Update the portrait* uses what was found. A
read that fails is never retried by itself: only this does it.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: A position of the profile's `work` list.

200.description: The wizard's state, with that employer's new state.

put.summary:
Type a past employer's own website. Nothing is read until the portrait is
made again (`POST …/portrait?again=true`).

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: A position of the profile's `work` list.

post.summary: Turn what the person wrote into proposed changes to the profile.
post.description:
**One model call.** Each change quotes their words; a claim their words
do not say, or a quote that is not theirs, is a flag, shown and never
dropped. The changes also add sentences to the portrait, as *told*. A new
submission replaces the changes the last one made. Nothing is saved yet.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: A language tag such as `pt-PT`; English when left out.

200.description: The wizard's state, with the changes.

post.summary: Make the portrait, or take the one made for this profile version.
post.description:
Reads the latest five employers' own websites first (only where a site is
known; cached 30 days), then makes the portrait: **one model call** per
profile version, plus one per employer read. The model never sees the
person's name or contact details. Every `known` or `told` sentence is
checked against the sources it cites; one that fails is downgraded to
`assumed`, never dropped.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: A language tag such as `pt-PT`; English when left out.

parameters.name: again
parameters.description:
Make the portrait again, even though one exists for this version
(after an employer's website was added).

200.description: The wizard's state, with the portrait.

post.summary:
"That's enough for now": no more questions; on to the review. No model
call.
